issues.title: P0: EVOLVE must drive sustained nonrepeating musical development across all intentions and 8 roles
issues.body:
## Owner hardware requirement — mandatory corrective release
**EVOLVE cannot merely show a variation percentage or occasional random notes.** The user should be able to set EVOLVE controls and hear genuinely creative, harmonious, constantly renewing musical development over long sessions while maintaining song identity and each intention's style. Changes in EVOLVE must be audible and traceable on the requested animated real-time EVOLVE graph ([issue #4](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/4)).

## Source audit
Published [v0.6.0 `device/dsp/engine.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/dsp/engine.c) `trigger()` has probabilistic phrase changes gated by `e->variation`, `e->freeze`, absolute step/loop boundary, plus section/phrase choices. But this is **not proof** of coherent sustained progression/anti-repetition for all 8 roles or meaningful distinct control over macro musical development. `device/ui.c` exposes VARIATION, ENERGY and FREEZE; current EVOLVE tabs are LOOP/EDIT, NEW SONG/EDIT, GROOVE/EDIT. The preexisting `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` explicitly calls for 3–8 hour music progression and accessible evolution controls; audit any implementation already done rather than repeating it.

## Required capabilities
1. Clear EVOLVE panel with immediately discoverable controls: **EVOLUTION LEVEL = Stable / Subtle / Flowing / Adventurous**, variation intensity, **SECTION / PHRASE** display, pace of change, optional role Hold/Follow/Evolve, Freeze/Unfreeze, next variation / next section, 16/32/64 loops. Explain differences in plain language.
2. **Macro evolution**: multi-minute changing arrangements, intro/build/resolve/rest/return, textural density, evolving energy and intentional breakdowns/rebuilds; coherent with the chosen intention, instrument role patch, drum kit and nature/FX palette. Never let progression be just a repeated 16-step phrase with occasional random pitch substitutions.
3. **Meso evolution**: motifs remembered, transformed, variation/repeat, call-and-response, complementary evolving piano/arps/chords and changing bass/drum patterns; frequent enough to hear, paced by selectable evolution level and current intention.
4. **Micro evolution**: subtle accents, velocities, note spacing, timbral motion and phrase articulation that are restrained when the mode is Stable or low-energy. Higher intensity must create meaningfully more musical variation, not simply loudness, density or random key changes.
5. **All 8 roles** (Lead, Bass, Pads/Drone, Harmony, Piano, Plucks, Choir and Drums) must evolve distinctly and musically. Bass moves beyond repeating tonic, drum patterns/fills/ghost hits evolve without unintended aggressive percussion, pads/choir morph chord/entrance, melodies build recognizable leitmotifs.
6. **Intention/style awareness**: keep musical identity, corresponding patches/kits/Nature/FX, scale, 432/440, chosen reference HZ and binaural channel separation stable. Never change exact reference frequencies. Respect all track locks, manually selected patches/kits, Nature Auto/Manual/Off, Freeze, solo/mute and saved banks. EVOLVE must not unilaterally reset style or override user decisions.
7. **Long-session memory**: bounded fixed-size motif/section/drum/bass histories to avoid obvious repetition, allow motifs to return after meaningful variation. Deterministic reproducible seed behavior, sensible 16/32/64-step structure and seamless transitions, no hung notes or endlessly increasing memory; save/restore the evolution state where appropriate.
8. **Real-time EVOLVE graph:** animate actual section/phrase state, role activity, bass/drum changes, requested/observed motif transformations, upcoming transitions and Freeze/Lock; every knob adjustment visibly changes its accurate model, with audible result. No fake graphs or frozen generic art.
9. **Tests**: multi-seed, every 13 intentions, all 8 roles, all loop lengths, all evolution levels incl zero and freeze, dynamic patch/kit/nature/style changes, New Song/Reroll Sounds semantics, manual locks, stop/start, 3–8-hour accelerated simulation and long PCM listening checks. Measure event-sequence uniqueness, motif retention/recall, section diversity, CPU/FX p95/p99 and XRUN delta. Verify 0% or Stable actually produces stable patterns, higher intensities demonstrate meaningfully more evolution without chaos.
10. Preserve beautiful existing musical balance and optimize performance using low-cost control-rate scheduling, **not per-sample additional algorithmic cost**. Cross-reference optimisation #7, sound library #6, UI #2.

## Evidence and release
Create a concise before/after timeline of musical changes per role, A/B listening samples for every evolution level, animated EVOLVE emulator recordings and hardware test checklist. Hardware artistic acceptance belongs to owner. Complete in next versioned corrective release without modifying published 0.6.0.

issues.title: P0 next build: AQUORA Dreamcast-inspired intro — AQUORA Sans title reveal + original ambient FM sound
issues.body:
## Owner's updated November 5, 2026 hardware feedback — overrides previous Game Boy concept
The owner hears **no intro sound effect** when starting AQUORA v0.6.1. They now want a memorable **original, ambient FM-synthesized startup inspired by the spacious, mysterious, cinematic feel of the Sony PlayStation 1 boot experience**, rather than the prior Game Boy-style chime. Keep the intro **8 seconds**, visually display the saved visualizer and selected panel theme, and instantly skip on any knob/button/key.

This supersedes the old Game Boy sound reference completely. Compose **new music and sound design**, not a copy of Sony's protected startup recording, distinctive melody, or exact sonic sequence.

### Source-confirmed investigation starting point (published v0.6.1)
- `device/app.c::app_render()` contains an intro `bell` generated with **two high sine partials** using `fm_sinf(t*2764.6015f)` and `fm_sinf(t*4160.1589f)`, with ~3s `intro_samples` gate, amplitude multiplied by `intro_gain` and `output_gain`. It is a tiny stereo-identical bell, **not an actual multioperator FM-ambient orchestration**, and may be barely audible in the actual speaker chain.
- `intro_samples` counts sample frames and stops after 3s even though intro visuals run 10s in actual published v0.6.1. `app_input_only()` still uses `now-intro_start>=10000u`; issue #8's 8s request is **not implemented yet**.
- `output_gain` follows the physical `master` value and resets to zero at master=0; `intro_gain` also becomes zero at master=0. Check whether inaudibility is caused by master volume, first startup audio/DMA initialization, timing (3s chime expired before ready), routing/codec/speaker/headphones, mute, amplitude, accidental skip or another actual bug. **Do not assert a diagnosis before testing**.
- Current bell has **no true FM operator modulation**, no evolving low tone, no spatial motion or ambient tail, and does **per-audio-sample `fm_sinf`** calls. Given reported default v0.6.1 overload immediately after flash, new intro must be extremely cheap and isolated from the general 16-voice instrument engine during startup.

### Required new sonic identity — self-composed, FM-native, 8 seconds maximum
- A low, soft, mysterious **FM shimmer and resonant swelling chord** rises out of near-silence; gentle harmonic metallic/glass tones bloom into an original signature interval/motif; warm diffuse airy tail resolves peacefully into AQUORA. A sense of scale and wonder, but characteristically **AQUORA's own unique brand identity**, not an audio replica of PlayStation, Sony, Nintendo, or another startup.
- Within 8s with clear presence on the FM-1 speaker **and** headphones at normal listening volume. Do not rely on deep subbass inaudible on tiny speakers; include balanced midrange, smooth harmonics and sensible levels. Remain refined, never an aggressive blast.
- Use existing sine LUT / very lightweight 2-op FM phase accumulation, 2–4 bounded voices max, control-rate envelopes, precomputed coefficients and extremely cheap stereo widening appropriate to hardware; no new large PCM asset or reverb buffers. A subtle lightweight single-tap stereo tail or efficient reuse of available stable send path; never initialize full expensive effects solely for the intro.
- Separate **intro elapsed time** (wall-clock ~8s) from **audio start time** (when the audio pipeline is actually ready). Trigger a clearly audible onset once output is ready and fit the motif into the remaining intro window instead of wasting its first seconds during device initialization; avoid playing late after user skips.
- Seamless synchronization with visual startup (current Original or Polar Bloom preference), matching swells to crystal/geometry blooms without expensive continuous extra geometry or background telemetry.

### Physical controls and safety
- **Skippable immediately** by *any knob, button, or key*, consume skip input to prevent accidental transport/patch changes or surprise notes; graceful ~20–80ms audio fade, no pops or leaked FX after skip. Stay compatible with watchdog/recovery/update startup.
- Honor **hardware master = 0 as silence**, and an optional saved Startup Chime OFF / Quiet / Normal setting that is obvious and not duplicated elsewhere. Do not force sound when user explicitly muted, and never start with unsafe fixed high output volume. Provide clear on-device option to enable/disable. Avoid accidental skip due to jitter in analog master-reading unless there was an intentional input edge.
- Store overall 8-second intro duration and startup setting correctly with versioned migration, preserving existing settings/LED/banks/visualizer theme; no per-frame flash writes.

### Acceptance/tests before next corrective release
1. Programmatically capture the **actual device PCM/DAC feed** from startup after device init and verify nonzero expected waveform on active volume, not merely a simulated oscillator, across master level settings, speaker vs headphones routing and audio pipeline startup timing; verify zero samples when muted.
2. A/B test v0.6.1 current intro vs new FM intro for loudness (safe peak/RMS), audible midband content, envelope shape, absence of DC/clipping, predictable 8s duration, graceful skip/fade under every input, and no post-intro audio tail/leak.
3. Provide a short listenable WAV from the exact firmware synthesis path and emulator startup video preview with audio, with test results attached to GitHub Actions.
4. Compare CPU overhead and callback p95/p99, first-boot-after-install performance, extra FX use, XRUN delta vs no-intro, and memory. **No regression to default PLAY** (#12).
5. Physical FM-1 speaker/headphones sound acceptance remains **owner-unverified** until tested; cite only verified software evidence.

### Scope and relationship
Update the intro feature tracked in this issue instead of adding another overlapping issue. Keep selected visualizer persisted (#16), styled panel themes (#16), visible fullscreen recovery (#14), hidden graphics gating (#15), post-install first PLAY issue (#12), optimization (#7). Work's next versioned corrective release must include this before declaring intro complete. Do not modify published v0.6.1 or any in-progress concurrent Work checkout. Status: **requested, not implemented**.

issues.title: P0: Full-project optimization, deduplication and safe cleanup before next corrective release
issues.body:
## Owner directive — mandatory whole-project optimization pass (next AQUORA corrective build)

During this corrective build, perform an **end-to-end optimization, deduplication and safe cleanup pass** across the entire firmware project: source code, DSP/music generation, FM synthesis, drum engine, Nature Beds, FX, visualizers, dynamic SOUND/EVOLVE graphs, UI/navigation, LEDs, BLE/AIR, memory, assets, toolchains and build/release files. Remove code/assets/dependencies that are provably obsolete, unused, redundant or duplicated. Do **not** delete historical GitHub backups, published release assets, recovery/update tooling, licensed notices, or any reachable functionality simply because it looks old.

**Optimization is part of acceptance, not an optional later pass. Preserve all features the owner likes and the new requirements tracked in issues #1–#6.**

### 1 — Establish a reproducible baseline
- Start from the latest verified GitHub source and tagged published 0.6.0 baseline; use isolated GitHub Actions runners, not the blocked shared Work lock. Confirm a single release publisher.

### 2 — CPU/DSP, FX and generator
- Refactor heavy per-sample work into cached values, lookup/interpolation, control-rate updates, preplanned steps/events where **audibly and numerically equivalent**; minimize repeated trig, exp, divisions, branches, redundant mixer passes, denormal work and excess voice/FX processing.

- Profile new lightweight 2-op FM paths / resonant percussion and realistic procedural/compact-sample Nature Beds so they do not overwhelm audio. Never silently reduce sound quality or delete unique usable patches in the name of optimization.

### 3 — Memory, graphics, UI and LED handling
- Bound buffers and reduce duplicate tables, recomputation and temporary copies; check worst-case RAM/stack and overflow bounds on FM1 hardware targets.
- Optimize the Original and newly requested second Vizz-inspired visualizers: fixed-bounded vertex/particle counts, cached geometry, efficient depth ordering/projection, dirty rectangles/partial LCD updates where safe, no excessive memory bandwidth, core-1 worker where hardware validated and safe core-0 fallback.
- The live SOUND/EVOLVE audio-accurate graphs must use **bounded, decimated, lock-free telemetry** rather than heavy DSP copies or fake motion. Keep UI editable/responsive under max load; graph OFF must not incur ongoing cost.
- Implement efficient LED event update masks/brightness and music-reactive Dance mode with low CPU/power burden; fix On mode and no stuck state.

### 4 — Code, build, asset and dependency cleanup
- Build an inventory of reachable modules/controls/assets, duplicate helpers/tables, unused debug/test-only production code, unused images/audio, dead branches, stale docs, obsolete build outputs, redundant archives, risky macro/constant duplication and unreferenced dependencies.
- Verify reachability via build/linker maps, source references, firmware feature matrix and emulator UI paths **before removing any production file or symbol**. Archive or retain test fixtures needed for regression. Respect GPL/MPL/third-party attribution and pinned SDK provenance.
- Replace duplicated logic with one well-tested implementation where practical; use clean interfaces and ensure compile-time/runtime feature flags behave consistently in native, forced single-core, host emulator, and recovery/installer builds.
- Prune **only generated or genuinely obsolete build products from the active tree**, never historical GitHub releases or source backups without explicit owner instruction.
- Maintain accurate, short current build queue and release docs: do not mark work complete on intention alone; cite changed files, tests and measured improvements.

### 5 — Required validation and proof
- Run incremental targeted tests while optimizing, then **full final acceptance** against all features and issue #1–#6 requirements. Include reproducible A/B PCM audio and output behavior comparisons, deterministic song selection/locks/migrations, Nature/FX stereo/level checks, over-time evolution, old/new UI control navigation/mutation, LED outputs, BLE/AIR simulated paths, save/load, release updater, native and forced single-core, WASM/emulator, installer and long-duration stress.
- Supply a compact *before/after scorecard* with CPU/audio/FX p95/p99, XRUN delta, flash/RAM/binary size, graphics work/frame timing and artifacts. Do not claim improvement where data is missing; call out tradeoffs.
- Any cleanup that causes audio artifacts, missed LCD updates, altered tuning, inaccessible controls, bank incompatibility, update failure or other regression must be reverted or fixed.
- Final target is **measurably leaner and more stable** with maximum verified headroom, not simply fewer lines of code; do not invent a performance gain. Hardware AIR responsiveness, delivered LCD FPS, DMA stability, physical LED behavior, physical-key feel and sound quality await owner's FM-1 verification.
- Preserve published v0.6.0 and v0.5.0 rollback. Publish the next versioned corrective release **only after** matching code, tests, archives, checksums and live installer are verified.

## Execution style
Work in coherent batches with independent reproducible GitHub Actions; avoid old shared lock and wasted duplicate testing; checkpoint compactly to GitHub. No need to stop at intermediate subgoals. Mark this issue complete **only after an optimization report and end-to-end verified release artifacts exist**.

issues.title: P0: Expand FM-based sound library — intention-aware FM patches, drum kits, and natural ambience beds

**6 FM melodic patches** (at least): **Moon Glass Keys** (soft 2-op FM bell/piano), **Halo Choir FM** (breathy gentle evolving tones), **Silk Harmonics** (slow glowing inharmonic pad), **Rain Harp** (plucked gentle FM), **Deep Resonant Bass** (smooth subtle FM sub layers), **Velvet Reed FM** (expressive woody wind/reed).
**4 FM-influenced drum kits** (at least): **FM Moon Kit** (soft round kicks/sine pitch sweeps), **Temple Resonance** (gentle low toms and tuned metallic taps), **Warm Pocket** (soft analog-FM kick/snare), **Stardust FM** (airy percussion with bell-like accents).
**4 extra Nature Beds** (at least; naturally coherent, not all FM): **Florida Night** (insect/frog chorus, distant ambience), **Twilight Meadow** (sparse layered songbirds, leaves and insects), **Crystal Creek** (water babble, natural trickle with occasional soft resonances), **Mountain Rain** (soft distant rain/wind, irregular drips). Use FM where it contributes naturally to insect tones, resonances or subtle textures; use filtered noise/compact legally licensed nature recordings or procedural hybrid for realistic environmental sound. Avoid pure beep-based bird/frog sounds.

## Engineering requirements
1. Build **actual lightweight FM operator synthesis** (prefer one/two modulator operators and simple bounded parameter envelopes using reused phase state/LUT, not new costly per-sample trig/exp). Provide programmable carrier/modulator ratio, modulation index/envelope, brightness/tone, decay/release, and gentle detune, with conservative CPU bounds. Consider that v0.6.0 already uses up to 16 voices; do not force FM on every role or replace existing loved sounds.
2. Evaluate ways to reuse existing `sr_voice.phase/phase2` where safe, but don't break current glide, vibrato, voice stealing and saved bank behavior. Ensure no per-sample dynamic allocation, expensive trig or unexpected DC/clipping.
3. Drum FM topology: short enveloped pitch/mod-index sweep for kicks/toms, softer inharmonic sidebands for tuned taps, mixed with existing bounded noise for shakers/brushes. Preserve existing Drum Presence/Level/Density/HIT distinction and the ability to mute/solo.
4. Nature Beds: make their behavior more believable with variable sparse phrases, multi-layer dynamics, gentle stereo spatial movement and longer nonrepeating evolutions. Provide bounded active nature voices, quiet gaps and realistic transients. Reuse/amend issue #5 realism acceptance. The user values sound first; prohibit a costly sample decoder or additional long-running effects without profiling.
5. Integrate **intention AND musical-style-aware selection**: for each of 13 intentions, define compatible weighted instrument patches (per role), drum kits, Nature Beds and related FX/energy settings, with variability by mood/style/tempo and deterministic seeds. Preserve user patches and explicit MANUAL/LOCK/OFF. New Song should coherently reselect unlocked sounds; Reroll Sounds should not rewrite motifs; EVOLVE should preserve song identity. Avoid hard-coded `0..7` and other old library bounds in UI/engine.
6. Keep published v0.6.0 patch IDs, kit IDs, Nature IDs and saved-bank compatibility stable; append IDs or build explicit versioned migration. Audit all constant sizes, `uint8_t` IDs, arrays, UI names, Quick Find, bank serialization, host tests, manual and firmware package.
7. Every new patch, kit and Nature Bed needs an **instant audible preview** and an appropriate **live SOUND graph** (actual signal and/or accurate parameter preview), direct editability and discoverability from the redesigned UI. Different patches/kits must genuinely sound distinct, not just have different labels.
8. Hard limits and performance: 44.1 kHz, 256-frame callback ~5805µs, 16-voice dense arrangement, max drums, Nature Beds and FX, single-core fallback and UI activity; profile mean/p95/p99 + XRUN delta + peak/clipping against v0.6.0. Reduce complexity and/or voice count of new sound paths if insufficient headroom; never knowingly reduce audio stability.
9. Produce level-matched A/B renders of old and new patches/kits/beds, selection-matrix tests for all 13 intentions with multiple seeds/styles, audible distinctiveness tests, long-session nonrepetition/locks/Off/persistence tests, emulator previews, native/single-core firmware acceptance and packaged checksum proof. Physical listening and actual FM-1 load remain owner-unverified until their testing.

## Release
Preserve the v0.6.0 tag and v0.5.0 rollback, stage into the next **versioned** corrective release and GitHub Actions CI. Don't describe this feature as completed until code, tests, actual generated selections, UI access and matching release artifacts exist.

issues.title: P0: Make Nature Birds and Forest convincing — eliminate synthetic repeating chirps and noise beds
issues.body:
## Owner hardware feedback (AQUORA v0.6.0)
The current **Birds** and **Forest** Nature Beds sound artificial/cheesy. Improve realism while preserving AQUORA's soft, musical, therapeutic-ambient atmosphere, and maintain strict FM-1 CPU and memory headroom.

## Source-confirmed cause
In [`device/dsp/engine.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/dsp/engine.c), `bed()`:
- Uses one PRNG white-noise sample per audio sample and first-order filtered noise for wind/rain.
- For bed type 4 (Forest) or 6 (Birds), emits a recurring decaying single-oscillator chirp:
```c
if(e->bird_wait)e->bird_wait--;
else { e->bird_env=1.f; e->bird_wait=SR_RATE+(rng(e)&65535u); }
e->bird_env*=.99985f;
e->bird_phase+=(1700.f+800.f*e->bird_env)/SR_RATE;
float bird=sine(e->bird_phase)*e->bird_env*.085f;
```
- Forest = filtered wind + this chirp; Birds = chirp only. There is no distinct bird species phrase, layered ambient ecology, stereo movement, wind foliage or realistic timbral variation. A single repeating chirp pattern is likely to sound electronic.

## Required improved Nature engine
1. Design **realistically varied, natural and gentle soundscapes**: multiple distinct birds (short separated phrases with species-like interval, chirp type, pitch curve, duration, resonance and silences); forest with rustling canopy, soft wind in leaves, sparse distant wildlife/insects and subtle spatial depth.
2. Prefer **properly licensed field recording snippets** for authenticity if storage/flash, codec/resampling and performance budget allow. Record exact source licensing/attribution and verify packaged assets; do not silently use unlicensed samples or huge PCM banks. If samples exceed constraints, implement carefully profiled lightweight procedural/compact hybrid synthesis with multiple naturalistic phrase templates and formant/noise components.
3. Vary density and time of day/scene character; realistic quiet gaps, occasional overlapping but sparse calls, foreground/background distance and naturally irregular intervals, no identical loop or cheap electronic beep, avoid constant loud/high frequency bird calls.
4. Maintain true stereo ambience when headphones are attached, gentle random position/pan, mild room/environmental color and level matching; avoid excessive reverb or masking the music. Don't let bird pitch tracks reference/solfeggio note frequencies unless deliberately designed musically, and never change fixed frequency or binaural separation.
5. Use efficient control-rate event scheduling and lightweight voice count/decoders with bounded memory and DSP cost. Compare Nature OFF / Birds / Forest under 16 voices, max drums, reverb/delay, stereo binaural and visual graphs; no new XRUN/clipping/regressions. Nature OFF must be near-zero overhead.
6. Coordinate with [Issue #3 — Intention/style-aware automatic Nature Beds](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/3): AUTO selects appropriate intensity, species/ambience palette by intention and style, MANUAL preserves user choice, OFF truly silent, and crossfades smoothly between scenes. Don't rewrite previous locks or re-enable intentionally disabled Nature.
7. Add easy **SOUND > NATURE** live audition and controls for bed, level, character (Birds/Forest), activity/density, proximity/distance, and mute/Auto/Manual/Off state; avoid overwhelming complexity, use sensible presets. Integrate with the graphical SOUND editor and Quick Find.
8. Deliver A/B audio samples (old/new, level-matched), representative long listening render samples, deterministic variation tests, and owner hardware listening checklist. Show reliable objective behavior in code and listening evidence; a test that only confirms output is nonzero is insufficient.

## Acceptance
Birds sounds like gentle environmental birdsong instead of a repeated synth chirp; Forest sounds like an actual layered natural setting rather than wind + beep. Preserve the appealing musical engine/FX and source/versioned backups; publish only as part of verified corrective release.

issues.title: P0: SOUND + EVOLVE dynamic audio-accurate interactive graphs, replacing static visuals
issues.body:
## Owner request (AQUORA corrective release)
Stop showing frozen/static visualizer artwork on SOUND and EVOLVE. These pages should use **impressive, continuously animated, audio-accurate interactive graphs** that visibly and instantly respond as each knob is turned or a parameter is edited.

## Published 0.6.0 source audit
- [`device/ui.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/ui.c) `PAGE_SOUND&&group==0` caches a **129-point** oscillator shape plus 129-point envelope, recomputing **only** when patch/tone/attack/release values change. This is a static parameter preview, not the continuously running audio waveform.
- Most non-PLAY content otherwise routes to `geometry(band*48)` (common decorative visualizer); EVOLVE has no dedicated timeline/role graphs of current generated changes.
- [`device/dsp/engine.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/dsp/engine.c) provides musical engine state and post-fader meters, but a true live scoped waveform must be extracted from an actual selected-track or mix signal, not fabricated from parameter values alone.

## Required SOUND interface
- Replace static art with a large animated **oscilloscope** (selected instrument/role and optional full mix), with a smooth trace showing actual note waveform/amplitude or a clearly labeled synthetic patch-model preview when real capture is unavailable.
- Provide an explanatory **envelope/shape graph** overlay: attack, decay/release, brightness/filter, glide/vibrato, pitch motion, pan/FX wet/send, harmonics and any actual editable parameter that applies to that role. When parameters have no time-domain interpretation, use a truthful companion plot (response curve, spectrogram-like band bars, panning meter, stereo L/R, reverb/delay history), not a misleading redraw of the same waveform.
- Immediate knob-to-graph and knob-to-audio feedback; large parameter name/value units and highlighted K1–K4, with a helpful graph legend (dry/wet, input/output, expected/actual).
- Do not fake graph reactivity: sampled trace only when genuinely derived from audio, envelope curve from actual envelope math, spectral/energy bars from measured cheap band data or clearly labeled approximations. Show silence and muted roles accurately.
- Provide useful selectable graph types by editing context (OSC/ENV/MOTION/FX/MIX) rather than burying parameters in unrelated screens. Keep graph legible at 240×240 and controls easy to locate.

## Required EVOLVE interface
- Replace static artwork with a live scrolling **arrangement/phrase timeline** showing real current step/bar/section, 16/32/64-step loop, note/event density per role, actual drum hit pattern, bass movement, melody motif signatures/variations, dynamic energy, transitions and pending evolution events.
- Link knobs for Evolution Level, variation, groove, freeze/lock, motifs and role-specific settings directly to clearly animated indicators. Distinguish observed events from scheduled/planned events.
- Display changes immediately when NEW SONG / REROLL SOUNDS / EVOLVE actions occur and correctly preserve frozen/locked role indicators.
- Meaningful visual motion even during quiet portions without inventing musical events; restrained luminous quality, consistent AQUORA design language.

## Technical performance requirements
- Audio timing takes precedence. Use bounded, lock-free/control-rate telemetry: decimated stereo/track samples or low-cost ring buffer captured from existing DSP paths, cached/precomputed geometry, small fixed line counts, staged partial LCD updates, core-1 geometry where truly available. **No blocking allocations, locks, FFT or per-pixel glow in the 44.1 kHz real-time callback**.
- Measure real cost vs prior build in 16 voices, max drums, Nature, AIR idle/on, FX on, visuals ON/OFF, single-core fallback; monitor callback p95/p99, XRUN delta, UI responsiveness and actual delivered LCD FPS (physical test remains owner's).
- Support 20 fps targeted on hardware without claiming host frames prove delivery. Navigation and parameter edits remain responsive with the graphs active.
- Automated host tests validate sample telemetry correctness, parameter mapping, frozen/muted states, live rendering progression, graph bounds/clipping, performance budgets, save/reload behavior, and zero changes to actual audio when the graph is disabled.
- Supply **short looping emulator previews and real 240×240 snapshots** showing an audio waveform animating and several knobs changing the associated graphs.
- This is distinct from the independently requested Vizz.fm-inspired full-screen second visualizer. Both requirements must be satisfied.

## Acceptance
Owner can visually identify how **each parameter changes the actual sound or arrangement** without guesswork. The graphs must demonstrate live behavior and true DSP linkage, not a stylized static image or cosmetically oscillating curves. Preserve source and versioned firmware; include in next corrective release.

issues.title: P0: Intention- and style-aware Nature Beds — automatic coherent selection, overrides, and smooth evolution
issues.body:
## User requirement (AQUORA corrective release)
The Nature/Soundscape Bed must be chosen **automatically according to the selected intention, musical style/character, instrumentation, energy, rhythm, arrangement, and frequency/reference context**, so each generated song feels like a coordinated musical environment. It must be easy to see, hear, change, lock, or disable the chosen bed.

## Source audit — published v0.6.0
[device/dsp/engine.c](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/dsp/engine.c):
- `sr_set_scene()` assigns `e->bed_type=sr_scenes[scene].ambiance` when Nature isn't locked. This is only a single default by intention.
- `sr_generate_song()` has `palette[SR_SCENES].beds[3]` and weighted choice **only if** `!(e->sound_locks&SR_SOUND_NATURE) && e->bed_type && e->bed_level>0`; it is predominantly intention plus RNG, with no distinct musical-style-aware model.
- Nature uses eight choices listed in [device/ui.c](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/ui.c): `Off, Wind, Water, Rain, Forest, Ocean, Birds, Leaves`.
- [device/app.c](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/app.c) `case 21` sets Nature bed manually **and unconditionally sets** `SR_SOUND_NATURE` lock. There is no obvious complementary `AUTO BY INTENTION + STYLE` status, easy unlock, or separately persistent "Nature OFF by user choice" handling in the current feature.
- No independent musical-style field exists in the released DSP engine. Style should be properly modeled, not falsely inferred from a fixed 4-flavor sound pool.

## Required corrective behavior
1. Define coherent, expressive **Nature palette profiles for all 13 intentions**, refined by explicit musical style/character (when available), tempo/energy, instrument roles, generated arrangement/phrase, and musical texture. Preserve intention's sonic purpose; don't treat selected Hz as proof of medical effects.
2. On selecting an intention or **New Song**, automatically choose a **compatible Nature Bed**, level and appropriate texture/FX ambience by weighted, reproducible rules. Ensure audible and visually clear differentiation with multiple seed variations. Use common lightweight beds, no costly repeated resampling/voices/FX.
3. Add **Nature Selection: AUTO (Intention + Style) / MANUAL / OFF** with obvious status and one- or two-action route through SOUND/NATURE and Quick Find. A manual selection stays fixed until consciously set back to AUTO. OFF stays silent and is never forcibly re-enabled by New Song, intention change, bank load, or song evolution. Consider separate Nature Enabled, Mode and Locked Bed state so Off is not conflated with "current bed ID = 0".
4. When selecting new intentions/styles, make coherent, gentle, **click-free crossfades** instead of abruptly swapping bed type or modifying unrelated settings. Support controlled slow organic changes over long sessions where appropriate; avoid random loud swaps.
5. Honor frozen arrangements, locked sources, saved banks, legacy migration, user volume, mute/solo/source isolation, return to the same settings after power cycle, and strict performance stability. Nature bed should neither override tuned frequencies/binaural separation nor compete excessively with music.
6. Provide clear UI display of `Nature AUTO / MANUAL / OFF`, currently chosen bed, sound level, compatibility reason or theme, preview/audition, and available bed choices. Update concise device manual.
7. Add deterministic tests across **all 13 intentions**, multiple seeds and styles, AUTO/MANUAL/OFF transitions, repeated New Song, arrangement evolution, restoration, save/reload, no surprise re-enable when off, and transitions under 16 voices + max drums + FX. Log actual chosen bed IDs and levels and compare representative audible PCM. Maintain audio/DMA headroom.
8. This requirement is coordinated with intention-specific patches/drum kits and the interface overhaul: a **single coherent song-profile system** should drive patches, drums, Nature, motion and FX—not disconnected RNG picks.
9. Never mark completed merely because `sr_set_scene` assigns a bed ID; require tests + emulator UI + owner FM-1 listening acceptance.

## Release handling
Correct in the next **versioned** release; do not silently mutate published v0.6.0. Preserve existing sounds/firmware and rollback, use independent GitHub Actions, avoid repetitive unrelated tests.

issues.title: P0: Full FM-1 interface discoverability/editability audit — every implemented AQUORA parameter reachable
issues.body:
## User hardware report (AQUORA v0.6.0)
The UI remains too difficult to navigate. Users cannot readily locate and edit all available features/parameters. Existing Quick Find provides a list of categories, but its route tests are not equivalent to exhaustively verifying editable destinations.

## Current evidence

## Corrective requirements
1. Enumerate **every implemented parameter** and UI action from actual sources (`app.c`, `ui.c`, `engine.c`, saved settings, mixer, patch editor, MIDI/Bluetooth, AIR, nature, generated styles, frequencies, visualizer, FX, drums, banks, LEDs, performance). Identify each control ID, value range, saved scope, display name, navigation path and K1–K4 input mapping.
2. Construct a searchable/readable **Settings Directory / Quick Find** that takes users directly to the *editable* parameter, not merely a broad page.
3. Consistent top-level page navigation, SELECT focus, group/tab switching, EDIT actions, back/Home, transport-safe controls and visible context. Eliminate hidden controls, unintended mode changes and stranded settings.
4. Optimize frequently used settings to roughly 1–3 understandable actions: intention selection, role/patch, tone/attack/release, drums and kit, soundscapes, Frequency Lock/HZ, binaural, FX, AIR, visualizer presets, mixer/solo/mute, banks, LEDs, performance.

8. Preserve the musical engine/sound and previously verified features; avoid broad rewrites that introduce audio instability. Supply emulator walkthrough screenshots and owner FM-1 hardware usability checklist.

## Acceptance
A source-to-UI requirements matrix has no implemented feature lacking a named, functioning navigation/edit path; real user's common edits can be done without a manual. Do not declare complete solely because previous 17 navigation routes passed. Include in next versioned corrective release.

issues.title: P0: LED On mode fails to illuminate key LEDs; redesign lighting behavior and test real FM-1 outputs
issues.body:
## User hardware report (AQUORA v0.6.0)
When **LIGHTS = On** on the physical M-VAVE FM-1, the user sees only PLAY and RECORD button lighting; the other expected key/button LEDs do not light. LED lighting needs substantially improved behavior and clearer modes.

## Source finding
In [`device/app.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/app.c), `app_input_only()` constructs:
```c
unsigned buttons=(engine.running?(1u<<B_PLAY):0)|(engine.freeze?(1u<<B_SEQ):0);
unsigned lights=k;
if(pending&&pending<=NKEYS)lights|=1u<<(pending-1);
if(lighting==3&&engine.running)
  for(unsigned t=0;t<SR_TRACKS;t++)
    if(engine.tracks[t].meter>.045f)
      lights|=1u<<((engine.tracks[t].events+t*3u)%NKEYS);
plat_leds(lighting==1||lighting==2?0:buttons,lighting==2?0:lights);
```
`device/ui.c` labels mode indices `On, Keys, Off, Dance`, but in **On** mode the key mask remains only *held keys plus pending key*, not *all fitted key LEDs*. This is a source-confirmed mismatch between label and behavior. The platform FM1 driver supports `plat_lights(buttons,keys,dim_buttons,dim_keys,glow)`, `plat_lights_mid`, `plat_glow` and `plat_leds` (FM1-base `device/plat_fm1.c`).

## Correction requirements
- Audit the physical M-VAVE FM-1 LED matrix/pin mapping and which key/button LEDs are independently controllable. Do not assume physically nonexistent LEDs can light; use a diagnostic **LED TEST** that steps every supported key and button LED and logs the matrix slot.
- **On:** continuously illuminate all supported keys and relevant button LEDs at a sensible safe brightness; distinguish PLAY's red/green indicator and preserve meaningful transport feedback.
- **Keys:** responsive piano-key illumination on actual key presses and optional active-note feedback; ensure notes don't leave LEDs stuck.
- **Off:** switch off user-configurable decorative lighting, preserving only truly mandatory safety/transport indicators if needed, with correct labeling.
- **Dance:** expressive, clearly visible **music-reactive** illumination using actual note/drum/onset/role activity and bounded release/pulse patterns; not arbitrary near-invisible flashes. Respect timing, CPU and battery budgets.
- Optional user-selectable brightness/glow level if the platform supports stable values; no flickering or excessive power draw.
- Make settings self-explanatory in a **SETUP > LIGHTS** page, easy to access with Quick Find; show the active mode and exactly which outputs are controllable.
- Persist mode/brightness across restart and test saved-bank / 0.5.0 migration behavior.
- Add host tests covering output masks for all modes, a platform/emulator LED preview, and a **hardware test checklist** for every key/button LED and musical activity.
- Preserve existing 0.5.0 and published 0.6.0 artifacts. Include in the next versioned corrective release, not a silent replacement.

## Acceptance
On physical FM-1, selecting On visibly lights all supported key LEDs; Keys, Off, and Dance behave as named; no stuck LEDs, unintended recording-state changes or audio performance regression. Physical acceptance remains owner-unverified until tested.

issues.title: P0 next build: reconcile deferred work and enforce evidence-based requirement coverage (Visualizer 2 #17)
issues.body:
# Post-v0.6.5 requirement reconciliation — prevent omitted scope and duplicate work

**Owner directive, 2026-11-05:** Last AQUORA release missed a major second-visualizer redesign despite successful v0.6.5 software publication. Audit ALL previously requested tasks, especially deferred work, and make the next build reject unexplained omissions. Preserve accepted v0.6.5 software/installer, and respect exclusive build ownership.

## Verified root cause
- v0.6.5 accepted scope explicitly covered only **Issues #2, #16, #24, #26–#30 and draft PR #25**, see `validation/integration-065/REQUIREMENTS.md`. That does NOT include Issue #17's latest ground-up water/sand cymatics replacement brief.
- The repo's `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` then reported "no outstanding v0.6.5 software implementation" without a next-release carry-forward queue.
- 30 issues remained open (and 0 closed) as of the audit; some of these are software-complete and others deferred, partially implemented, or pending hardware aesthetic/listening checks. An unqualified open/closed flag is insufficient.
- Current main `device/visual_worker.c` still uses a **17×17 nodal field and up to 256 marching contour segments** in `resonance_job()`; `device/ui.c::visual_name()` still displays **Resonance Plate**. This is not the owner's requested distinct, organic water/sand system in [#17](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/17#issuecomment-6667383022). CPU-cost reductions in #26 do not count as completing #17.

## Current release scope — latest owner-authorized deferral

Approval: https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/31#issuecomment-6702097918 and https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/32#issuecomment-6702099240. This supersedes earlier USB-required wording.

| Requirement ID | v0.6.6 disposition | Carry-forward / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| MIDI-USB | OWNER-AUTHORIZED DEFERRED / not a release blocker | Revisit after KIRA-9 has a good working firmware build and owner reprioritizes. Preserve partial code; do not enable unfinished performance routing. |

All non-MIDI software acceptance, backups and publication gates remain mandatory. External MIDI clock/routing/interoperability acceptance is deferred with the transports. Preserve v0.6.5 and all completed work; KIRA-9 untouched.

## Reconciled queue — v0.6.6 software delivered (historical brief below)
- **P0 CONFIRMED MISSED:** #17 genuine ground-up second visualizer replacement: visible water ripples/standing-wave vibration and sand-like granular migration and settling along stable nodes, visibly distinct from Resonance Plate/Polar Bloom; accurate music onset, pitch, intention, frequency, silence and morph response; preview sequences for low/high notes, silence, formation, settling, transitions; owner aesthetic acceptance **UNVERIFIED**. No "cosmetic contour redesign" accepted. Prevent regression to 58ms draw/6ms geometry; render bounded, audio-first, native + forced-single-core fallback and measured host comparisons. User specifically forbids either visualizer on the public showcase gallery; keep branded spiral intro separate.
- **OWNER-AUTHORIZED DEFERRED:** #31 performance USB and BLE MIDI, per the current-scope matrix above; AIR remains required.
- **P1/P0 SUBJECT TO VERIFICATION:** #13 AIR usability (true packet/proximity feedback, accessible effect routing, no fake scanning), #18 muffled drum-kit owner listening findings, #9 fresh intention A→B→A variation incl unlocked patch IDs/evolution over sessions; consult latest source/tests and hardware observations before assuming a missing implementation. Do not override an already-proven fix.
- **EVIDENCE GAPS / targeted audit, not blanket rebuild:** #1 LED On (source now sets `all_keys`, physical matrix still unverified); #3 intention/style-aware Nature AUTO/MANUAL/OFF; #4 real SOUND/EVOLVE graphs and website APNG; #5 realistic Birds/Forest; #10 fullscreen frame occupancy; #19 website deployment (live publication json reports current site); #20 SAVE one-press; #21 visual themes; #22 v0.6.4 catch-all; #23 music modes + automatic glide/vibrato. Also inspect any other unresolved owner comments. Classify each as **Software completed / Partial / Blocked / Owner hardware unverified / Open** with evidence. Do not conflate a physical listening claim with a software test.
- **Already accepted software:** #2, #16 scoped typography/themes, #24, #26–#30 as specifically recorded in v0.6.5 acceptance; do not reimplement without concrete regression evidence. This does NOT waive remaining #16 subrequirements or physical acceptance.

## Mandatory prevention system — applies to both AQUORA and KIRA-9
1. Before build, generate a **single current requirement register** from root scope, active queue, every open issue and **latest owner comments** (including deferred issues and changes after previous release). One canonical ID for each distinct feature; deduplicate aliases while preserving all acceptance conditions.
2. Each requirement row: ID, current owner wording + source URL/comment, version introduced/targeted, priority, status (NEW / PARTIAL / COMPLETED SOFTWARE / BLOCKED / OWNER-UNVERIFIED), exact source file/function/commit, targeted automated test IDs, emulated visual/audio artifacts, physical test owner and explicit **carry-forward disposition**.
3. **Release blockers**: no unclassified issue/owner comment; no P0 row silently deferred; no row marked completed based on notes, code existing, mock tests, a rename or successful compilation alone. Design-heavy visual work requires before/after true 240×240 sequences with representative scenarios reviewed against the *latest* requested visual goal, not merely geometric-count or hash changes.
4. At end, compare planned vs actually delivered; **zero unexplained missing requirements**. For genuine deferral, record owner's accepted scope decision, explicit next version, current blocking rationale, and a visible NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE entry. A successful hotfix is not permission to declare the entire project backlog empty.
5. Compact `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` holds ONLY unfinished work, each with an ID/link; archive completed with source/test/release evidence in `CHANGELOG.md` / `validation/`. Synchronize GitHub issue states/comments as appropriate; don't blindly close issues with owner hardware checks pending.
6. Release gate script/CI should validate requirement IDs and traceability file: fail on missing status, missing P0 evidence, falsely completed items without commits/tests, incomplete carry-forward or stale release version. Add targeted negative test proving a deliberately deferred requirement fails if missing from the next queue.

issues.title: P0 next build: eight-role arrangement evolution, fading entrances/exits and inactive mixer tracks

## Owner-reported hardware observation — November 6, 2026

While watching the MIXER on the latest AQUORA firmware, the owner sees that **all eight tracks never seem to be used**: some tracks appear disabled, unassigned, or never generate audio over the entire listening period. This is an observational report, **not yet a verified root cause**. The latest build otherwise runs smoothly with no lag observed so far; protect that performance baseline.

## Required next-build investigation and fix

1. Audit the **eight intended musical roles, including drums**, their patch/kit assignment, generated phrases and evolution, and mixer track/bus mapping. Confirm whether all eight are configured, enabled, and capable of contributing in the default arrangement. Distinguish genuinely silent source roles from non-role buses and intentionally sparse musical rests.
2. Trace each role across generator selection -> note scheduling -> voices/voice stealing -> envelopes/FX -> gains/mute/solo/Auto Level/Auto Gain -> mixer meters -> DAC. Look for permanently empty/unassigned patches, zero gain, mute defaults, routing/channel mismatches, low priority voices, and UI meters that falsely imply inactivity.
3. Exercise **13 intentions × three music modes**, and **16/32/64** step loops, New Song, Reroll Sounds, Freeze/evolution, save/recall, STOP/PLAY, and intentional sparse arrangements. Ensure each role expected by the design becomes meaningfully active over a long enough interval, with musical variation and without mandatory eight-part continuous playback.
4. Add targeted role-activity diagnostics: per-role patch ID, enabled/mute/solo state, generated-event count, accepted voice count, post-gain signal level/peak and mixer meter identity. In automated renders, inspect both event counts and actual audible PCM per-role stems / sampled mix; distinguish silence caused by intentional arrangement from failure.
5. Fix proven defects **without** forcing all eight roles to sound in every bar, muddying arrangements, artificially inflating meters, increasing CPU/XRUNs, or regressing the owner's currently smooth v0.6.5 audio/UI performance.
6. Supply source+test evidence and before/after diagnostics, plus a short owner hardware acceptance checklist showing how to verify all eight roles on the FM-1 mixer. Mark physical confirmation **OWNER-UNVERIFIED** until tested.

**Priority:** P0 core generative audio role/track integrity for next build. Carry forward in `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` and requirement matrix Issue #32. Do not modify published v0.6.5 assets as part of this backlog note.

## Additional owner hardware feedback — dynamic track entrances/exits (2026-11-06)

Owner clarification: a generated song **typically uses the same ~4–5 musical tracks for the entire listening session**; those parts persist, while remaining roles stay silent from start to finish. The desired experience is a living arrangement: **different roles should gradually enter and leave as the song evolves**, with audible, smooth fade-ins and fade-outs rather than a fixed set of channels throughout the song.

### Acceptance criteria (added to existing P0 issue)

- Implement or verify a phrase-/section-level **role-activity plan** for all eight intended musical roles (including drums): rotate supporting parts in/out over time while retaining harmonic coherence, intention/style, recognizability and musical flow. Evolution should be perceptible across **16/32/64-step loops** and longer sessions.
- Support smoothly automated **per-role fade-in/fade-out envelopes** and appropriate transitions/crossfades on phrase or section boundaries (click-free, avoid abrupt re-entry, note tails/reverb handled gracefully); protect the audio-thread budget. Preserve musical rests and occasional intentionally sparse passages; **do not force eight simultaneous loud tracks**.
- Check whether silent roles result from generator assignment or eligibility, missing phrase triggers, role activation state, instrument selection, signal routing, or mixer metering; ensure that **each enabled, eligible role has a realistic opportunity to become audible during evolution**, not only when restarting or manually changing intentions. A permanently silent role should be explicable by a user mute/lock/intentional arrangement rule, not accidental omission.
- Verify gradual entrances and exits are reflected accurately in the MIXER: role meters track real post-gain signal and controls remain intuitive; no fake audio or artificially animated meters.
- Add extended deterministic scenario tests and per-role stem/meter timelines for 13 intentions × three modes, 16/32/64 steps, New Song/Reroll/Freeze, plus save/recall. Assert meaningful **variation in active-role sets** and transitions over a realistic multi-evolution duration, not merely a nonzero note for each track. Exclude deliberately frozen, soloed or muted roles from inappropriate assertions.
- Measure fade slopes, clicks, audible onset/decay, XRUN, CPU and visual responsiveness against v0.6.5; preserve the owner's current **no-lag** observation. Include explicit **OWNER-HARDWARE-UNVERIFIED** listening/mixer checks in the final acceptance notes.

This is a **requested next-build behavior**, not an implemented fix or evidence that the current generator is broken in a particular subsystem. Do not start a separate concurrent build or modify the current released firmware for this note.


## Owner clarification — musical discretion, not eight-track quota

All eight roles are **available**, but **they do not all need to play in the same song, at once, or even during one entire song**. The style, selected intention, chord/harmonic progression, musical phrases and evolving arrangement should organically determine which instruments enter, overlap, fade, depart, or remain silent. A beautiful sparse piece might use only a few. Some styles or evolutions may genuinely call for all eight. The failure to investigate is **permanently unavailable/nonfunctional roles or an unintentionally static 4–5-track configuration**, not a requirement to force every role into every composition. No arbitrary minimum-track quota or rotation timer. Test all eight roles' capability in suitable contexts and the musical appropriateness of transitions.

## Comparative engine review (2026-11-06)
Reviewed actual [SIREN 0.9.1 source](https://github.com/isod89/siren-fm1) and AQUORA's `device/dsp/engine.c`. The actionable original-design handoff is [validation/SIREN_GENERATIVE_ENGINE_REVIEW_2026-11-06.md](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/main/validation/SIREN_GENERATIVE_ENGINE_REVIEW_2026-11-06.md). Prioritize section-level role planning with intention/music-mode/harmonic context, optional gradual role fade entrances/exits, stable motif return, deterministic seeds and true post-gain audio/stem checks. SIREN demonstrates style-weighted forms and section-aware note gating; its code does **not** demonstrate the desired continuous eight-role crossfade system, which AQUORA must design independently. Respect SIREN's GPL-3.0-only copyright conditions; do not copy source/tables/assets without distribution-license review. Research only, no firmware implementation or release claim.

issues.body:
## Owner physical FM-1 request — Nov 7, 2026 — all modes, including master level zero

> "all visualizer should react much more to the audio, and even [if] the volume is set to 0."

This is an explicit **cross-mode** requirement: **Original** (Mode 1), preserved **Cymatics** (Mode 2) and planned **Chladni** (Mode 3, #36) must show substantially clearer, musically meaningful motion. **Turning the FM-1's physical master volume knob all the way to zero must NOT stop or suppress visualization while the AQUORA transport/audio engine is still producing music internally.** Visually silent != acoustically muted.

### Exact audio signal contract (avoid false triggers)
- Drive visual animation using **internal pre-physical-master / pre-speaker-output** signal telemetry: audio energy / RMS, transient/onset strength, per-role audible contributions, harmonic/pitch context and optional spectral proxies from the engine **before hardware master attenuation**. Preserve proper **post-track/solo/arrangement-gain** semantics: a muted or inactive role should not create fictitious "audible" visual peaks; external audio if actually routed through engine can be included when available. Effective internal mix can still animate while headphone/speaker output is muted.
- Physical master **0% vs 100%** for the same sequence should yield **equivalent visual motion** (apart from nondeterministic capture timing), despite exactly muted DAC output at 0%. This behavior should also hold during smooth changes of master while running and after saved preferences reload.
- No "visualization from the absolute constant animation clock only": rhythmic kicks should induce conspicuous but controlled impulses, bass should cause slower/heavier waves, melody pitches should affect motion/geometry, chords should generate coherent interference; quiet passages should be visibly calmer, and attack/decay should be observable. Keep the artistically distinct identities of the three modes.
- When **STOP** is pressed or engine genuinely silent, visual activity should **decay/settle naturally**, not keep showing full-volume musical excitation. Intentional reference/binaural/Nature layers may animate only when truly active internally. Preserve ongoing ambient ease; avoid frantic strobing / flicker and false “frequency healing” claims.
- Respect user-selected black/white background and improved white-theme contrast requirement #37. Preserve particularly the current **Cymatics Mode 2** black-background appearance, not replace it with Mode 3's nodal mandalas.
- Avoid additional DSP/heavy analysis in the real-time audio callback. Reuse existing pre-master track meters, `engine.master_peak`, role/onset/pitch telemetry as safe inputs or add lightweight bounded snapshots; use frame-domain smoothing/attack-release and separate geometry/render work, not FFT or costly sample-by-sample graphics.

### Current source grounding (v0.6.6)
- `device/app.c::app_render(...,master)` applies physical master in `output_gain` **after** `sr_render(&engine,pcm,n)`. The internal mix/telemetry therefore need not be tied to hardware master, but must be verified through end-to-end tests.
- `device/visual_worker.c::prepare_geometry()` samples `engine.tracks[t].meter`, role onset/events, pitch and engine frequency; `visual_job` uses meter to set Original petal radius and `resonance_job` uses meter/onset to drive Cymatics water/sand. They may need **higher perceptual dynamic range**, more transient response and more meaningful musical differentiation without driving overload.
- Do not fake a full audio response simply by cranking up static `energy` or decorative phase, nor derive visual amplitude from the post-hardware-master `lr[]` output buffer.

### Acceptance criteria and evidence
1. Deterministic/recorded **same internally generated musical sequence** at physical master 0, low, and high: output PCM muted at zero, yet per-frame visual telemetry and geometric reaction demonstrably equivalent. Also move master dynamically during PLAY; no discontinuity in visual response.
2. Contrast clips: kick/snare/percussion transients, solo bass swell/glide, lead notes, chord/polyphony, changing pitch & harmonies, loud-vs-soft, Nature-only, intentional silence, STOP and release tails. Every mode must show strong **observable correlations to music** and reasonable decay; no permanently animated noisy screen while truly stopped.
3. Validate all three modes in black/white themes and full-screen/PLAY; 240×240 genuine renderer captures/short animations for comparison, owner aesthetic approval pending physical device test.
4. Keep v0.6.6 smoothness and audio-first priority: host/native/forced-single-core tests, instrument frame p95/p99, FPS/XRUN safety, DMA ownership; robust fallback if load high. No additional full-screen redraw per sample, preserve battery and display responsiveness.

**Expected:** "Next build for AQUORA should remember some basic things on shutoff, like which visualizer you selected." This must also work if the user changes the visualizer **while music is playing** and subsequently powers off without pressing STOP.

Do not add broad indiscriminate writes; verify each preference has intentional save/load semantics.
- **Do not persist automatic live drum/FX arrangement values as global device preferences.** User explicitly wants drum settings to initialize from suitable defaults at reboot and to be chosen automatically **when an intention/music style is selected** (#40). Four saved arrangement banks are independent and must restore their explicitly saved song states when the user chooses a bank.
- Avoid banking side effects: **loading/saving/replacing a bank must not unexpectedly overwrite the globally preferred visualizer** unless the user explicitly chooses to restore a bank's visual setting. Current `device/arrangement.c::arrangement_apply` sets `visual_mode=record->visual`; document and correct precedence.
- Preferences should survive an abrupt ordinary device off after a recent edit (within an explicitly bounded commit window) **without requiring the user to stop PLAY** or perform an undiscoverable save. Provide visible confirmation such as brief "Preference saved" when meaningful; no excessive indicator clutter.

### Source audit — v0.6.6
- `device/app.c::save_preferences` includes `settings.visual=visual_mode`, and `app_init` restores it *after* `arrangement_init` resets visual index. A formal persistence path exists.
- `device/app.c::app_frame` schedules `save_preferences()` only when `!engine.running&&!requested_play&&!engine.stop_frames&&!engine.external_audio`, after ~1200ms; therefore **a user editing during a long-running song then switching off cannot rely on it being saved**. This is a plausible root cause; verify on device/host rather than treating it as proven.
- `device/app.c` UI edit `control==38` currently uses binary `visual_mode=d>0`; update to 0–2 (same migration requirement as #36), with explicit navigation and readback.
- `device/arrangement.c` currently restores `visual_mode` on bank load; decide/document global-vs-bank precedence and test.

### Performance/flash safety
- No blocking flash write on audio real-time interrupt or long, audible XRUN-causing UI stall. Implement reliable, coalesced, wear-conscious and crash/power-loss-safe global settings storage consistent with FM-1 platform APIs; don't continuously write every knob tick. If the underlying platform cannot safely persist while playing, explicitly surface a reliable way to commit before power off and report limitation instead of falsely claiming persistence. Preserve v0.6.6 real-time smoothness.
- Verify power-cycle (not just app in-memory reinit), changing Mode 1→2→3 while PLAY, reboot after bounded idle, saved bank LOAD, fallback from malformed settings, 0.6.5/0.6.6 migration and direct updater, no false bank corruption, and 240×240 UI readback. issues.title: P0 next AQUORA: Make 16/32/64-step loops musically distinct—true multi-bar phrases, harmonies, bass/drum development
issues.body:
## Owner physical FM-1 test — AQUORA v0.6.6 (2026-11-07)
> "change from 16, to 32 or 64 should be more useful... right now i cannot really notice it doing anything... the patterns usually remain the same regardless, lets look into it."

**P0 musical-functionality quality gap**: 16/32/64 LOOP STEPS should produce audibly and meaningfully different phrase architectures, not merely altered loop-wrap/evolution timing or slight variation of one 16-step idea.

### Source-based diagnosis (v0.6.6 `aquora-next-integration`)
- `device/dsp/serenity.h` stores only `melody[16]` and `motif_home[16]`, irrespective of `loop_length`.
- `device/dsp/engine.c::motif_degree(e,step)` indexes `melody[step & 15]`, with a small bar-based pitch-degree transform for second/further bars. This cannot independently compose full 32-/64-step call/answer sections on its own.
- `trigger` builds `idx=loop_pos`, sets `s=idx` for 32/64 but uses **absolute step** for 16. This creates counterintuitive differences: multi-loop 16 can continue bar-dependent progression while longer lengths wrap `s` within their block; for many step gates/events `s & 15` stays identical on each bar. Different wrap timing alone is not enough audible distinction.
- `drum_trigger` and other role note gates use `step&15`; higher bars only have minor additions/accents. `mode_phrase` uses a four-slot progression but insufficient shared per-bar compositional contrast. The existing macro-role system (#34) has independently probability-gated roles rather than planning intentional complementary bar/section functions.
- `sr_set_loop_length` queues a new length until a loop boundary while playing. This is safe but can make the control feel unresponsive. The UI labels `NEXT LOOP STEPS` but a short, clear pending/applied indication and audible preview transition would improve understanding.
- Existing `tests/role_evolution_next.c` (117 scenario combinations) checks role targets, nonquiet role stems and fades; `tests/arrangement_roles_060.c` checks correct iteration counts, long scheduling and role event presence. **Neither establishes a perceptible distinct musical structure between same-seed 16,32,64**, so the owner's observation remains valid despite tests passing.

### Musical specifications by loop length
1. **16 — motif/groove:** one concise repeatable rhythmic/harmonic idea, coherent and suitable for steady meditation, with optional subtle fills and low-rate evolution; preserve current recognizable core motif as appropriate.
2. **32 — two-bar phrase:** deliberate first-bar statement and **second-bar answer/development**: differentiated lead/harmony contours, alternating bass movement, chord/pad voicings, tasteful drum answer/fills and short phrase resolutions. The second half must not be a simply transposed carbon copy of the first.
3. **64 — four-bar passage:** coherent **A / A′ / B / resolution (or intention/style-appropriate alternative)** with more distinct melodic development, bass progression, sustained textures/choir motion, varied percussion articulation, intentional accompaniment entrances and closing fill. Avoid arbitrary dense chaos or forcing all eight roles to sound simultaneously.
4. **All 13 intentions × 3 music styles:** the level/pace of contrast must reflect the intention and style. Some can be minimal and spacious, others more expansive, but **every longer setting needs noticeable multi-bar identity**. Preserve correct scale/tonic, exact reference Hz, binaural separation, smooth texture changes, FX/Nature behavior and human listening serenity.
5. **Musical form above loop length:** distinguish **pattern length** (how many steps a phrase spans) from **macro sections** (arrival/bloom/rest/breakdown/return) and **EVOLVE PACE/VARIATION** (how often and strongly themes transform). Work with #34 macro song-form improvement so drums don't randomly fade simply due to a role coin toss. Maintain stable motif memory and tasteful return.
6. **Switching while PLAY:** length update at next safe boundary with visible current vs pending value; preserve musical continuity (no unexpected motif reset/stuck notes/FX cuts), change actually audible in the next matching phrase, obey STOP/freeze and explicitly saved banks. Add small contextual "1 phrase / 2 phrases / 4 phrases" labels if possible without UI clutter.
7. **Implementation:** design compact, original, deterministic, seed-stable per-bar phrase variations / response and harmonic-state plans; avoid expensive real-time generation, RAM/flash bloat or copying SIREN GPL code/assets. Reuse existing 16-step motif memory as source material but add a proper higher-level plan for 32/64, with graceful solo/mute and sound locks.

### Mandatory evidence and acceptance
- Controlled **same seed, intention, music mode, instruments, variation level** A/B/C recordings for 16/32/64, preferably isolated stems + full mix and score/event timelines. Compare distinct melodic note-degree sequences, bass/chord changes, drum hit maps and onset/gain per bar. Assert **meaningful musical sequence differences and higher-order development**, not just that role events exist or step counts differ. Keep music coherent; don't assert a fixed Hamming distance without listening context.
- Tests 13 intentions × 3 music modes × 3 lengths with variation 0/Stable and flowing/high, freeze, save/recall, returning motif, pending length changes while playing, New Song/Reroll, long sessions with section return; verify deterministic plan and click-free transitions.
- Full native + forced single core + emulator and hardware acceptance checklist; preserve v0.6.6 smoothness, screen performance/headroom, no XRUN regressions. Owner will physically judge whether longer lengths sound unmistakably richer.

## Owner design correction — NEXT BUILD (after v0.6.5 audio/visual stability gate)

**Owner is not satisfied with the v0.6.4 secondary visualizer, “Resonance Plate.”** It is **not** what they envisioned. This is a *replacement design brief*, **not** an instruction to refine the existing 25×25 contour mesh, polish its colors, animate more of its lines, or reuse Polar Bloom. ### Desired visual result — actual cymatics principles made beautiful

The user’s reference is **cymatics: sound vibrations made visible through physical media such as water and sand**. They want to *see physical matter organizing into resonance*, not a generic wireframe, radial ornament, oscilloscope, or abstract kaleidoscope.

1. **Quiet nodal lines vs active antinodes:** At standing-wave resonance, areas with little motion (nodes) become stable lines/contours, while high-motion regions (antinodes) visibly vibrate. Make this distinction apparent even to someone unfamiliar with cymatics.
2. **Sand / Chladni appearance:** Fine particles bounce, migrate out of vigorously moving areas, and **settle into crisp nodal lines**—complex, symmetric geometric networks that visibly **emerge from motion** rather than appearing as pre-drawn neon strokes. Believable granular accumulation, pattern formation and reconfiguration matter more than particle-count realism.
3. **Water appearance (primary visual inspiration):** Imagine a shallow illuminated dish / reflective water surface with concentric and intersecting ripples whose standing-wave interference **forms luminous geometric/mandala-like structures**. The water itself should shimmer and ripple at active areas, while stabilized nodal structures emerge. Reflective, vibrant, polished and organic; visually satisfying at actual 240×240 RGB565.
4. **Frequency and resonance behavior:** Lower pitch/low-order modal response favors simpler broad shapes (crosses, a few lobes/rings or sparse nodal curves); higher pitch / higher-order response **can** produce denser flower/snowflake-like networks. **Patterns sharpen and visibly “lock in” when a selected resonance mode is excited**; when pitch/notes/texture change, the pattern should bloom, deform, dissolve or reorganize coherently. This is an artistic simulation with grounded wave logic, **not** a claim that all frequencies universally produce one fixed geometry: physical plate shape, medium and actual resonant modes also determine patterns.
5. **Real music drives it:** Use actual instrument activity (especially bass, lead, harmony, piano and percussion onsets), note pitch/frequency, dynamic envelopes and intention/reference frequency to influence mode selection, energy, pattern complexity and transitions. Music rests should quiet the medium. A static preselected geometry with superficial oscillation is **not accepted**.
6. **Visual tone:** Original, immersive, beautiful, organic and colorful; smooth emergence of reflective water / settling fine sand; creative inspiration from real cymatics experiments and Masaru Emoto's imagery as *art only*, with **no unsupported scientific/therapeutic assertions**.

## Owner FM-1 test — K3 CALIBRATE switches to READY and remains there (Nov 5, 2026)
Owner attached a photo of AIR screen and reports: turning **K3 CALIBRATE** makes its status remain **"Ready"**, yet there is no clear feedback that proximity is sensing a hand, what FX is being modulated, or whether the radio is receiving signals.

**Verified v0.6.1 source explanation**:
- `device/ui.c`, control 68 displays `air_sensor.calibrated?"Ready":"Turn right"`.
- `device/app.c`, control 68 calls `aq_air_calibrate(&air_sensor,plat_ms())` on positive turn.
- `device/air_sensor.h`: calibrate stores an RSSI reference and sets `calibrated=1` if filtered is nonzero and last signal <800ms. `aq_air_update()` zeros stale `filtered/raw` after 800ms, **but never resets `calibrated`**.
- Thus Ready is only a **latched successful baseline capture indicator**, not proof that the radio remains active, is receiving packets, hand proximity works, or FX output moves. The UI needs **separate CALIBRATED and SIGNAL LIVE statuses**. Do not mislabel successful calibration as continuous AIR readiness.
- K1's 'Scanning' indicates only `air_on`, and `air_packets` is reset each 80ms `plat_air_sample` poll (not a stable cumulative/second packet count). So a '0' can be transient and the current UI provides insufficient evidence.

**Mandatory correction**: visible animated live signal/proximity bar with raw & filtered RSSI trend, packet rate over a stable 1–2s window, last packet age, baseline reference, live 0–100 modulation value, selected FX and actual wet parameter; meaningful states 'LISTENING', 'NO BROADCASTER', 'CALIBRATED – WAITING FOR SIGNAL', 'ACTIVE', 'SIGNAL LOST', 'RADIO ERROR' and explicit manual FX fallback. Add Far/Near guidance and thresholds/hysteresis, signal timeout handling. On loss, show calibrated baseline stored but ***not*** active; smoothly return FX to safe neutral, never stick on last wet unexpectedly except explicit Hold mode. Verify packet path on actual FM-1; initial calibration success may indicate recent RF data, **not** successful hand sensing. Full Korg Kaoss-inspired effect selector/presets still needed.
